payload.previous_feedback: Previous vetter reason: The proof correctly establishes integer-translation invariance of E(n,x) by applying the floor shift identity termwise and observing exact cancellation of the added nz terms. It matches the lemma statement and uses only permitted reasoning.
payload.previous_proof_nl:
Fix an integer n>1, a real number x, and an integer z. We prove that E(n,x+z)=E(n,x), where
E(n,t)=\lfloor nt\rfloor-\sum_{k=1}^n \frac{\lfloor kt\rfloor}{k}.

Using this definition,
E(n,x+z)=\lfloor n(x+z)\rfloor-\sum_{k=1}^n \frac{\lfloor k(x+z)\rfloor}{k}.
For the first term, since nz is an integer, the floor-translation identity \lfloor u+m\rfloor=\lfloor u\rfloor+m for real u and integer m gives
\lfloor n(x+z)\rfloor=\lfloor nx+nz\rfloor=\lfloor nx\rfloor+nz.
Likewise, for each k=1,2,\dots,n, the number kz is an integer, so
\lfloor k(x+z)\rfloor=\lfloor kx+kz\rfloor=\lfloor kx\rfloor+kz.
Substituting these identities into the expression for E(n,x+z) yields
E(n,x+z)=\bigl(\lfloor nx\rfloor+nz\bigr)-\sum_{k=1}^n \frac{\lfloor kx\rfloor+kz}{k}.
Split the sum:
E(n,x+z)=\lfloor nx\rfloor+nz-\sum_{k=1}^n \frac{\lfloor kx\rfloor}{k}-\sum_{k=1}^n \frac{kz}{k}.
Since \frac{kz}{k}=z for every k, the last sum is \sum_{k=1}^n z=nz. Hence the added nz terms cancel:
E(n,x+z)=\lfloor nx\rfloor-\sum_{k=1}^n \frac{\lfloor kx\rfloor}{k}=E(n,x).
Therefore E(n,x+z)=E(n,x) for all real x and all integers z.
